risk_if_not_implemented: Without Developer Screening, applications may be built and deployed with exploitable design and coding weaknesses that adversaries can leverage. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Excessive or Unauthorized Privilege (R-AC-2), Unauthorized Access (R-AC-4), Loss of Critical Knowledge / Capability (R-PE-1), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9), Workforce Shortage / Loss of Critical Skills / Labor Disruption (MT-25).

compensating_control_1.name: Personnel Screening
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to manage personnel security risk by screening individuals prior to authorizing access.
compensating_control_1.justification: Personnel Screening (HRS-05) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Developer Screening (TDA-19) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with People applicability. Given the people-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Third-Party Personnel Security
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to control personnel security requirements including security roles and responsibilities for third-party providers.
compensating_control_2.justification: Third-Party Personnel Security (TPM-13) provides third-party oversight that compensates for the absence of Developer Screening (TDA-19) by extending security obligations contractually and monitoring third-party risk in lieu of direct control. Given the people-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
